html:
On the last Sunday of Advent in 1511, the Dominican friar Antonio de Montesinos preached a sermon in Santo Domingo condemning the Spanish settlers for their cruelty to the Taino. "Are these not men?" he asked.

The settlers held the Taino in the encomienda system, forced labour that was killing them. Montesinos told his listeners they were in mortal sin. The colonists complained to the king, and Montesinos went to Spain to argue his case.

The dispute led to the Laws of Burgos of 1512, the first Spanish laws on the treatment of Indigenous people. Among those changed by the friars' preaching was the settler Bartolome de las Casas, who became their great defender.
